mhc_export.assay__comments: The binding of the epitope to HLA-A*0201 was determined using an MHC exchange fluorescence polarization assay. Peptides with substitutions of all 20 amino acids on all 9 positions were analyzed to determined the substitutions that enhance binding affinity. Substitution of Thr at position P(C-1) to Pro or Gly and substitution of Val at P6 to Ala, Asp, His, Leu, Met or Ser increased binding affinity the most (76% inhibition increased to 79-87%). Most substitutions of Leu at position P(C) decreased binding. Positions P1, P2, P3 and P(C-2), P(C-1), P(C) were also substituted with nonproteogenic amino acid derivatives.

reference_titles: Altered peptide ligands revisited: vaccine design through chemically modified HLA-A2-restricted T cell epitopes.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The binding of the epitope to HLA-A*0201 was determined using an MHC exchange fluorescence polarization assay. Peptides with nonproteogenic amino acid derivative substitutions at positions P1, P2, P3 and P(C-2), P(C-1), P(C) were analyzed to determined the substitutions that enhance binding affinity. In general, preferred modifications on P1 included am-phg, O-methyl-l-serine (SOME) and S-methyl-l-serine (CSME), and L/d-(racemic) phenylglycine (Phg). On anchor position P2 residues NLE, NVA, and 2-AOC resulted in higher-affinity APLs. Unsaturated amino acids propargylglycine (PRG) and allylglycine (ALG) were the best improvements on anchor position PC.

mhc_export.assay__comments: The epitope bound to HLA-A*11:0, as shown by MHC stability ELISA of peptide exchanged into UV-sensitive HLA-A*11:01 molecules. The epitope in complex with HLA-A*11:01, isolated for crystallization, was analyzed by size exclusion chromatography. The epitope occupied two alternative conformations in the crystal. Optimization of the size-exclusion protocol demonstrated that the two refolded A*11:01 complexes could be separately obtained. These molecular species did not interconvert when left in solution, and they had hydrodynamic volumes of 98 Å and 171 Å, as judged by dynamic light scattering, which likely correspond to the monomeric and dimeric MHCs, respectively.
